items.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023
items.q: With Stan Kenton you know I was with the mellophone band and playing lead trumpet with four mellophones, five trumpets and five trombones is kind of a chore.

ctx.x: Did you see into the — well you’re a young man and you’re thinking this is going to be my career, what are my opportunities here? What should I look to be doing?
Well I had my eye set on — I got the tail end of the big bands. I played — maybe you know this — when I was 13 I played a solo with Stan Kenton’s band and Ray Anthony © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

and different bands that came to town featuring Easton’s young trumpet player. Anyway then I think maybe you know this too, in that band that I played with that was Maynard and Buddy Childers and Conte Candoli — all the heavyweights you know — Bob Cooper, Art Pepper, all those guys. And I saw those guys get on that band bus and man I was drooling. I said I’ve got to get on that band bus someday. So I wanted to be a lead trumpet with that band someday. And it came to pass.
